clue.text: Bill in work is a different man!

indicators.note: the bill is placed inside the word for work

parts.note: a job is a piece of work
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone has changed completely after being taken on as a worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the man's name in the surface, but it is an invoice; AC (account) is the crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob is a male given name, the biblical patriarch among others.

clue.text: Nigel's seen about one

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the name are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S taken as a letter

explanation.surface: A man called Nigel has been spotted hanging around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NIGELS; here the possessive S is needed as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means just one, as in a single ticket.

clue.text: Key to fire engine?

parts.note: reads as a fire brigade vehicle's key, but means the key that sets a motor engine firing

explanation.definitionFit: The ignition is the switch, worked by a key, that sparks a car engine's fuel.

clue.text: He mingles with the crowd to get food

indicators.note: mingles suggests the letters are mixed in among one another

explanation.surface: A man mixes with the masses in order to find something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mingles' mixes HE with CROWD; 'with the' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, typically of fish or clams.

clue.text: Five hundred wrongly laid off-it's a bloomer

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: wrongly signals the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Five hundred workers have been unfairly made redundant, and it is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' signals the anagram of the two words; 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A daffodil is a spring flower, and a flower is something that blooms.

clue.text: Tell people you've had enough, then keep quiet

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a polite refusal of more and a hint that nothing more needs saying.

clue.text: Having a faraway look?

parts.note: reads as gazing dreamily into the distance, but means considering matters that lie far in the future

explanation.definitionFit: To plan with the distant future in mind is a figurative far-sighted outlook.

clue.text: Lady seen at Mothers' meeting

parts.note: ma is an informal word for a mother
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A woman spotted at a gathering of mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe lets 'Mothers'' stand for two different mothers, a human and an animal one, joined ('meeting') side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a woman.

clue.text: Obstinate but practical person, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a doer is someone who gets things done

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn but hands-on, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour describes someone stern and unyielding.

clue.text: See 7 across
Do wrong from start to finish

parts.note: off can mean from, as in buying something off a friend
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone gets everything wrong, beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' is just a joining phrase between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to commit a wrong or break a law.

clue.text: One still is first to make a snowman

indicators.note: is first says the word for still comes at the front

parts.note: yet means still, as in not yet gone
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is still the first to build a snowman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is first' puts YET before I; 'snowman' is the Abominable Snowman, not a garden figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the Abominable Snowman of Himalayan legend.

clue.text: They may give me a lord's estates

indicators.note: may give suggests these words could produce something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Land holdings that might make the speaker a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl's lands and rank are his earldom, so several are estates of nobility.

clue.text: It's sinful the silly way Grace lies

indicators.note: a silly way of arranging the words means their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about how a woman named Grace tells untruths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly way' rearranges GRACELIES; 'Grace' looks religious but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrilege is the violation of something holy, a sinful act.

clue.text: Young Italian graduate doctor in love

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A newly qualified doctor has fallen for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is Italian for a baby or small child.

clue.text: Amused by cunning devices in a plot

indicators.note: the devices are placed inside the plot

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground
guile is crafty trickery

explanation.surface: Entertained by a scheme's clever tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a plot' looks like a scheme but is a garden plot, BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to charm or divert, so beguiled means entertained.

clue.text: Urchin learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: A street child studying in order to go begging.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to plead earnestly.

clue.text: Girl compelled to take a job

parts.note: made means forced, as in made to go
a line is a line of work

explanation.surface: A young woman forced into employment.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeline is a female first name.

clue.text: They go along with kinky corsets

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Companions who accompany some risque underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Escorts are companions who accompany someone.

clue.text: Ships, and in them, pirates

indicators.note: in them says the word and goes inside the ships

parts.note: brigs are two-masted sailing ships

explanation.surface: Vessels with buccaneers aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigands are bandits or outlaws, much like pirates at sea.

clue.text: Dandy heard to grind his teeth

indicators.note: heard signals the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: gnash means to grind the teeth

explanation.surface: A fop was overheard clenching his jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash was an 18th-century leader of fashion in Bath, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard 'Beau' Nash was a famous Georgian dandy.

clue.text: Title of pantomime?

parts.note: reads as the name of a show, but means an honour also borne by a stock comic character

explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime, a Christmas comic stage show, the Dame is a woman played by a man; Dame is also a knightly honour for women.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's honorific and the drag role in festive stage comedy.

clue.text: Japanese ruler OK amid chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An emperor is fine in the middle of turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado is an old title for the emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Work to make some dough

parts.note: reads as earning money, but means pressing bread mixture with the hands

explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working flour mixture with the hands to form it.

clue.text: They fight with one another

parts.note: reads as foes clashing, but means partners fighting on the same side

explanation.definitionFit: Allies are nations or people united to fight side by side.

clue.text: No silk is used in these waterproof garments

indicators.note: used suggests the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: Rainwear made without any silk.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilskins are coats and trousers of oiled cloth worn against rain and spray.

clue.text: Makes eyes at a man on turning to leave

indicators.note: on says the man is added after
turning means the word for leave is read backwards

parts.note: go means leave
Les is a man's name

explanation.surface: Flirts with a man as she turns to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses only the word for leave; 'on' places the man after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone with desire.

clue.text: Can't hear notes fade away

indicators.note: away suggests the letters are sent off in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone unable to hear musical notes as they fade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges NOTESFADE. The definition is a verb phrase standing for 'is completely deaf'.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally lacking hearing means one cannot perceive sound at all.
